message.content:
Roger presented today for his initial intake session, reporting that he is currently not feeling his best and is experiencing significant distress due to difficulty focusing. He described a pattern where when his concentration feels "off," a wide array of other symptoms also feel amplified, leading to increased anxiety and depression. His self-reported GAD-7 score was 2 and PHQ-9 score was 3, indicating mild symptom severity, though he emphasized that the cognitive fog is particularly troubling for him.

The intervention used included active listening, psychoeducation regarding the relationship between focus difficulties and mood symptoms, and collaborative goal-setting. Roger responded well to the non-judgmental approach, showing willingness to engage in the process despite his initial hesitation. He disclosed that he is currently staying at Turning Point Shelter and collecting disability benefits for a Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI). We also discussed his history of substance use; while there is no current desire to use, Roger acknowledged that past usage caused substantial problems, reinforcing his motivation to maintain sobriety.

Roger’s response to the session was positive, as he expressed relief in having a structured space to discuss these challenges. He identified improved focus and reduced anxiety as primary goals for upcoming sessions. The therapeutic alliance appears solid, with Roger demonstrating openness about his shelter status, disability benefits, and substance use history without resistance. We will continue to monitor his mood and cognitive symptoms while building on the foundation of trust established today.
